sources.note: UNESCO synthesis of six forts, varied Rajput states, settlements, trade, production, learning, religion, art, music, and water harvesting.

sources.title: The Jantar Mantar, Jaipur

sources.title: A Court Beauty

sources.title: The Bhomias

proposedOverrides.summary: Atlas-audited Rajput states, communities, daily life, crisis, achievement, and continuity from 1800 to 1815.

batchIdentityNotes: Rajputs is an atlas aggregate and ethnosocial label, not one sovereign country or one identity shared by all residents.
The sole target polygon includes major Rajput capitals but also Bharatpur, Gwalior, and Bhuj, while excluding nearby Delhi, Indore, Ahmedabad, and Multan.
The 1783 start control groups most future member points under mahratta-states and Bhuj under sind-1783; neither is treated as an exact predecessor government.
At 1815 all sampled member points move to maratha, a gross atlas simplification that predates most Rajput-state protective treaties of 1817 and 1818.

Court paintings and chronicles are used as bounded evidence for elite settings, never as universal descriptions of farmers, artisans, servants, women, children, Bhils, Jains, Muslims, or other communities.
Krishna Kumari, sati, and jauhar are discussed without romanticizing coerced death or turning exceptional elite narratives into women's ordinary life.
